title: VQT-CiM: Accelerating Vector Quantization Enhanced Transformer with Ferroelectric Compute-in-Memory
problem: Transformer accelerators using non-volatile memory (NVM)-based compute-in-memory (CiM) for vector-matrix multiplication (VMM) face severe challenges: dynamic VMMs in attention (key-value operations) require expensive runtime write operations, compute-write-compute (CWC) dependencies, high write overhead, and limited NVM endurance degrade efficiency.
motivation: Transformers dominate NLP/CV but their massive memory bandwidth and power demands require CiM acceleration; however, NVM-based CiM lacks efficient support for dynamic attention computations.
method: VQT-CiM leverages vector quantization (VQ) of transformer keys and values to convert dynamic VMMs in attention into static VMMs with learned codebooks, eliminating runtime writes. Uses residual VQ (RVQ) + product VQ (PVQ) for enhanced representation capacity and maintains accuracy. FeFET (ferroelectric FET)-based CiM crossbars with optimized dataflow and peripheral circuits execute efficient codebook lookups and static matrix multiplications without write-back cycles.
key_novelty: Vector quantization scheme (RVQ+PVQ) that converts dynamic attention VMMs into static operations, enabling write-free CiM acceleration with ferroelectric memory.
contributions: Vector quantization method (RVQ+PVQ) for transformer keys/values enabling static VMM computation
Write-free CiM accelerator architecture using FeFET-based crossbars with static codebook operations
Optimized dataflow for efficient RVQ handling on CiM hardware
3.54× energy efficiency and 4.53× throughput improvements vs. NVM-based CiM transformer designs
limitations: Evaluation limited to transformer models; applicability to other architectures with dynamic weight matrices not discussed; quantization-induced accuracy loss details limited.
primary_theme: Write-free CiM transformer acceleration via vector quantization and ferroelectric memory
